answer: Each agent earns influence only through a unique, bonded signing key that must lock a scarce token for a cooling period before votes count. A registry rejects keys already linked to the same verified recovery credential, while slashing the bond when an agent double-signs. This makes a mirror identity visible and costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens for every additional persona, then risks losing them. The oasis of anonymity remains for ordinary activity, but not for multiplied governance weight; even a ferrous supply chain cannot make duplicate keys free.
